key_insight: LiteOdyssey shows that a single lightweight reasoning agent, guided by a diagnostic policy and public biomedical tools, can reach state-of-the-art rare-disease diagnosis without heavy scaling.
clinical_relevance: For rare-disease workflows, this could offer a more deployable and auditable AI assistant that helps prioritize diagnoses from clinical features alone.
method: Used Policy Iteration with Human Feedback (PIHF) to shape a clinical genetics reasoning policy.
Gave the model dynamic access to freely available biomedical tools during diagnosis.
Evaluated on rare-disease benchmarks using only patient clinical features, without fine-tuning or large retrieval ensembles.
evidence_signal: Across 1,243 cases from LIRICAL and PhenoPacket Store, LiteOdyssey achieved 59.3% Recall@1 overall, including 60.7% on the harder PhenoPacket subset versus 10.7% for the same base model without tools.
watch_item: Results come from benchmark and cohort evaluations, so real-world performance and safe integration into clinical review still need careful validation.
paper_title: LiteOdyssey: A Lightweight Reasoning AI Agent for Interpretable Rare-Disease Diagnosis
